title: Private market leaderboard: the companies at the top
summary: Anthropic and OpenAI now lead the private-company rankings, while AI, fintech and infrastructure define the rest of the field.
body:
Private-company valuations have become a moving target, especially in artificial intelligence. A recent ranking from Multiples places Anthropic first at $965 billion and OpenAI second at $852 billion, ahead of Tether ($500 billion) and ByteDance ($480 billion).

The point is not that these figures are permanent. They are reported private-market valuations, often set by the latest financing or transaction, rather than continuously traded public-market prices. Still, the list makes the current shape of private markets very clear: AI is pulling capital toward a small number of frontier-model, data, and infrastructure businesses.

At a glance

  • Anthropic: $965B valuation; $47.0B revenue listed.
  • OpenAI: $852B valuation; $25.0B revenue listed.
  • Tether: $500B valuation; $10.0B revenue listed.
  • ByteDance: $480B valuation; $186B revenue listed.
  • Databricks: $190B valuation; $7.0B revenue listed.
  • Stripe: $159B valuation; $6.9B revenue listed.
  • Waymo: $126B valuation; $400M revenue listed.
  • Revolut: $115B valuation; $6.0B revenue listed.

What the ranking says

Technology still dominates. The source estimates that roughly a quarter of the companies are AI-native, and that 52% are headquartered in the US. China contributes 14% of the list, led by ByteDance and a growing cluster of AI and fintech companies.

There is also a sharp difference between value and current revenue. The AI leaders command unusually high revenue multiples, while mature platform businesses such as ByteDance and Epic Games show the scale of revenue that can sit behind a lower multiple. That gap is worth watching: it captures both investors’ expectations and the risk that those expectations change quickly.

How to read the numbers

These figures are a snapshot, not an investment recommendation. Multiples says it compiles private-transaction data from public information, third-party APIs and manual verification, and converts figures to US dollars for comparison. Its ranking excludes acquired businesses and large family-owned groups with uncertain estimated values.

For company-specific research, the key question remains the same: what business model, revenue quality, and competitive advantage does the valuation assume?

brief.thesis: Private-market leadership is increasingly concentrated in AI, but the ranking also shows how different revenue scales and valuation multiples can be across private companies.
takeaways: Anthropic and OpenAI lead the ranking at $965B and $852B respectively.
AI, fintech, data infrastructure, and global consumer platforms make up much of the top tier.
brief.risk: Private valuations are intermittent and can shift materially between financing rounds.
brief.watch: New funding rounds, revenue growth, and any public-market listings that create clearer price discovery.

references.text: Ranking, methodology, and figures: Multiples, 50 Most Valuable Private Companies in the World. The source labels the ranking as August 2026 data and was last updated August 23, 2026.
